wu: Students play 'Two Truths and a Lie' about their life experiences. Each student writes three sentences about things they have/never have done, one false. They mingle, share, and guess the lie. Teacher models first: 'I have eaten camel meat. I have never been to Paris. I have climbed Mount Toubkal.'
wuAlt: Students complete the sentence frame 'I have never ____, but I have ____' with personal truths. They share with a partner.
Teacher shows 5 photos of activities (e.g., hiking, cooking, traveling). Students guess which one the teacher has never done using 'Have you ever ____?'
pres: Teacher presents 6 flashcards showing Halloween activities (carving pumpkins, wearing costumes, trick-or-treating). Models present perfect sentences: 'I have carved a pumpkin. I have never gone trick-or-treating.' Elicits forms from students: 'Have you ever...?' 'Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.' Checks understanding with thumbs-up/down for true/false statements.
presAlt: Teacher tells a short personal story about a Halloween experience using present perfect, then asks students to underline the target language. They identify the pattern.
Students read 3 short experience profiles (e.g., 'Fatima has celebrated Halloween twice.') and circle the 'have/has + past participle' structures.
prac: Students play 'Find Someone Who Has...' with a bingo grid. They mingle, ask 'Have you ever...?' questions (e.g., 'eaten Halloween candy?', 'worn a scary costume?'), and write names in boxes. First to get a line shouts 'Bingo!'. Teacher monitors and corrects pronunciation of 'ever/never'.
pracAlt: Students complete a gap-fill worksheet with present perfect sentences about Halloween, choosing between 'have/has' and the correct past participle (e.g., 'I have ____ (see) a ghost movie').
In pairs, students interview each other using a grid with 5 'Have you ever...?' questions about life experiences. They write down answers and report back to the class.
ls: Students listen to a 2-minute audio of two people discussing their Halloween experiences. They tick the activities mentioned (e.g., 'watched a horror movie', 'attended a party') on a worksheet. Teacher plays audio twice. Feedback: students compare answers in pairs, then class check.
re: After the break, students play 'Stand Up If...'. Teacher calls out experiences (e.g., 'Stand up if you have ever eaten Halloween candy!', 'Stand up if you have never worn a costume!'). Students stand up if true, stay seated if false. Quick energy boost.
prod: In groups of 3, students discuss 'Halloween: Commerce or Culture?'. They compare Halloween with local Moroccan celebrations like Eid or Aid Al Adha. Teacher prompts: 'Is Halloween just for shops? Is it like our holidays?'. Each group prepares a 2-minute summary to present to the class, using present perfect to share personal experiences (e.g., 'In our group, none of us has celebrated Halloween, but we have...').
rw: Students read a short article (100 words) about Halloween traditions in the US and Morocco. They underline all present perfect forms. Then, they write 5 sentences about their own experiences using 'ever/never' (e.g., 'I have never carved a pumpkin, but I have eaten Halloween candy.'). Teacher checks for accuracy.
st: Teacher tells a short, culturally respectful story about a Halloween misunderstanding in Morocco, focusing on experiences. Ends with the goodbye routine: 'Today we talked about our experiences using present perfect. Thank you for sharing, and have a great week!'
g: Students mingle, ask 'Have you ever...?' questions, and mark off squares on a bingo grid when someone says 'yes'.
Students walk around the class asking questions to find classmates who match specific experiences.
Students write three sentences about their experiences, one false, and others guess the lie.
Teacher calls out experiences; students stand if true, sit if false.
Groups debate if Halloween is commercial or cultural, comparing it to local holidays.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a short paragraph (3-4 sentences) comparing Halloween with a Moroccan holiday.
Support weaker learners: Use a sentence frame worksheet to write their 5 experience sentences (e.g., 'I have never ____ before.')
hw: Write a short opinion paragraph (80-100 words): 'Should Oujda celebrate Halloween? Give two reasons.'
Interview a family member about their experiences with celebrations (e.g., 'Have you ever celebrated Halloween?') and write 3 sentences in present perfect.
Complete a 'My Life Experiences' chart with 10 things you have/never have done, using 'ever/never'.
tip: Connect the grammar to their lives by using local examples (e.g., 'Have you ever eaten msemen on a holiday?'). This makes the target language more relevant and memorable for Moroccan learners.
